note: The answer key for the fixture. Sites are file and lines at each branch head; the scorer matches within a window.

defects.title: Every page of the transfer history drops its last item
defects.summary: transfersFor slices with an end of start + PAGE_SIZE - 1, so each page holds 19 items; the 20th of every page (indexes 19, 39, …) appears on no page, while total reports them all. The PR's test covers three transfers and page 2 of an empty tail only.
defects.failure: An account with 21 transfers: GET /accounts/:id/transfers?page=1 returns 19 items, page 2 returns 1; the transfer at index 19 is on neither page; total says 21.
defects.head: 5af451d1118a286fc59dd8d1ca957e4c5aebecf4

defects.title: The control-character test cannot fail, and the code alters the memo instead of refusing it
defects.summary: The new test wraps transfer() in try/catch and asserts only inside the catch, so it passes whether or not anything is thrown. Nothing is thrown: the code strips control characters and stores the altered memo, while the README and the PR say a memo with one is refused with 400.
defects.failure: POST /transfers with memo 'rent\u0000 due' → 201, memo stored as 'rent due'; the README promises a 400.
defects.head: 15dd7c4aaa0be03d4171fb77b94b233d29f75046

defects.title: openAccount's signature changed; scripts/seed.mjs still calls the old one
defects.summary: openAccount(store, { ownerId, label, actorId }) became openAccount(store, actor, { label, currency, ownerId }). The route and the tests were updated; scripts/seed.mjs, which the README tells a new install to run, was not, and nothing tests it.
defects.failure: node scripts/seed.mjs → TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'label' of 'undefined'; no accounts are seeded.
defects.head: ec38b7f4818c2cd7a7aee111ab72a7bfe1d786e7

defects.title: overdraftCents is never stored: the key is missing from SCHEMA, so pick strips it
defects.summary: Every write goes through pick(), which keeps only the keys SCHEMA lists, and SCHEMA.accounts was not given overdraftCents. setOverdraft's update and openAccount's insert both drop it silently; the response then shows overdraftCents 0 via the serializer's ?? 0, and a transfer that relies on the limit fails with insufficient funds. Migration 003 writes the key directly, but the first update of a migrated account strips it again. The README's own rule says to add the key to SCHEMA in the same change.
defects.failure: Admin: POST /accounts/:id/overdraft { overdraftCents: 500 } → 200 with overdraftCents 0; the stored row has no overdraftCents; a 300-cent transfer from that empty account → 409 insufficient funds.
defects.head: 88d0e534ac12020b2a6f616da97efb8b360d5676

defects.title: Relaxing getOwnAccount for accountants also lets them close and export any member's account
defects.summary: canSee() was added for the read routes, but it was wired into getOwnAccount, which closeAccount and the export route also use. An accountant, described as able to change nothing, can close any empty account and write any account's statement to disk. Only the two read routes are tested.
defects.failure: Accountant token: POST /accounts/<member's id>/close → 200, the account is closed; POST /accounts/<member's id>/export → 200, the CSV is written.
defects.head: 5ff5809a7176caf08fc66f3395df95848fca20e6

defects.title: An administrator's on-behalf transfer is recorded as the member's own act
defects.summary: The route passes the member as transfer()'s user so the ownership checks apply to the member's accounts, but transfer() also takes actorId and the audit entry's actor from that same argument. The transfer row and the audit log say the member moved the money; the administrator who did it appears nowhere. The test checks balances only.
defects.failure: Admin POSTs /transfers with onBehalfOf: <member> → the transfer row's actorId and its audit entry's actorId are the member's id, not the admin's.
defects.head: 5d9e288679769335a688cda4db28d8b2a64b4675

defects.title: The export file name is joined into the path unchecked: a name with ../ writes outside the export directory
defects.summary: name is validated for length only, then path.join(dir, `${name}.csv`) is written. A name such as ../../../tmp/x writes wherever the process may. The comment that guaranteed the file name was the account's id and nothing else was removed by this PR. The site is the unchecked join in export.js; the route's length-only validation is context, not a second site.
defects.failure: POST /accounts/:id/export { name: '../escaped' } → 200; escaped.csv is written beside, not inside, exports/.
defects.head: 036830a04e80ca63d934f178397b7d640e59d0cc

defects.title: Failed sign-ins log the Authorization header, bearer token included
defects.summary: The new warning prints ctx.req.headers.authorization whole. A mistyped or expired token, or a real one sent to the wrong environment, lands in the logs in clear, against the auth module's own comment that the token is never logged.
defects.failure: A request with Authorization: Bearer SECRET → the log line 'sign-in failed GET /accounts with Bearer SECRET'.
defects.head: 036830a04e80ca63d934f178397b7d640e59d0cc

defects.title: Withdrawals do not update the running totals, so the summary drifts from the accounts
defects.summary: deposit() bumps the currency's total; the new withdraw() changes the balance and records the audit entry but never calls bumpTotal. After any withdrawal the summary overstates the money held, for good. The tests check the summary after deposits only.
defects.failure: Deposit 100 then withdraw 40 → the account holds 60, GET /summary says AUD 100.
defects.head: 074592689156ce5df3f42042a91dffbd81dfed27

defects.title: The rename migration deletes label in the same step that writes name
defects.summary: docs/deploy.md: a migration is additive first and a removal ships separately, once no running copy reads the key. Two copies share the file during a deploy. Once 003 has run, the previous release reads account.label as undefined, and its pick() (SCHEMA with label, no name) strips name on its next write, so an account saved by the old copy during the window loses its name for good.
defects.failure: Migrate, then run the previous release against the file: every account's label is undefined; after the old copy saves (any transfer, close or deposit) the account has neither label nor name.
defects.head: 016008ca54a8acd3cc007b6c6c0ce2344685b86b

defects.title: The funds check and the debit straddle an await, so concurrent transfers overdraw
defects.summary: transfer() became async and awaits the screen between the balance check and the debit. Two transfers from one account interleave at that await: both pass the check against the same balance, then each writes a balance computed from the row it read before awaiting. docs/security.md: every path that moves money checks the balance it moves from at the moment it moves it.
defects.failure: An account holds $1,500; two $1,000 transfers arrive together. Both pass the funds check, both succeed; the account ends at $500, the receiver at $1,000, and $2,000 of transfers are on record.
defects.head: d8caf340eef7f0f44c72f131d3f6f4b042ef6810

defects.title: The list cache is cleared by transfers and deposits only; opening, closing and interest leave it stale
defects.summary: GET /accounts is cached per owner for 30 seconds and forgotten only in transfer() and deposit(). openAccount and closeAccount in accounts.js and the interest job in interest.js change what the list shows and never clear it. Main already invalidates the single-account cache through the store's change hook, which this cache does not use.
defects.failure: Open an account, list, open a second: the list still says one account for up to 30 seconds. Close one: it is listed as open. Accrue interest: the old balance is listed.
defects.head: f9885a2d214fad13783549473781a3855694632b

defects.title: The once-a-day guard compares the local day with a UTC day, so interest is credited every hour for part of each day
defects.summary: accrueInterest skips an account when lastAccruedOn equals today, where today is the local calendar day (toLocaleDateString), but it stores at.slice(0, 10), the UTC day. Wherever the local day differs from the UTC day, ten or eleven hours of every day in Sydney, the two never match and the hourly timer credits the account again each hour. The test pins noon UTC, where they agree.
defects.failure: TZ=Australia/Sydney, 07:00 local on 2 March (20:00 UTC on 1 March): three runs credit three days' interest; the hourly timer credits about ten a day.
defects.head: 0bf23917ade72ebeb93704c555a8504baff245e7

defects.title: Idempotency keys are global, so one user's key returns another user's transfer
defects.summary: remembered() finds a key by its value alone, not by the user who sent it. A second user who sends a key the first user already used gets the first user's transfer back as the response, with its accounts, amount and memo, and their own transfer silently never happens.
defects.failure: Member A transfers with Idempotency-Key 'order-1'. Member B posts their own transfer with the same key: B receives A's transfer as a 201, and B's money does not move.
defects.head: cc2c253bb916c2bb8b2d0ec72193e33814194eef

defects.title: The server sends requests to any http(s) URL a member supplies (SSRF)
defects.summary: setWebhook accepts any http or https URL and the notifier POSTs every event for the account to it from the server. A member can point it at internal addresses: cloud metadata, localhost services, the private network. docs/security.md: the service never requests a URL a user supplied.
defects.failure: A member sets http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ as the account's webhook; it is accepted, and the next deposit makes the server POST to the metadata address.
defects.head: f7520841c763d950e4f570b8a1092a58b1774f17

defects.title: The new readers ignore memo, so transfers written by the previous release lose their memo mid-rollout
defects.summary: The migration is additive and new transfers write both keys, but publicTransfer and the CSV export read only note. During the rollout the previous release still writes memo alone, and its pick() strips note, so every transfer it records shows an empty memo through the new release. docs/deploy.md: readers tolerate both shapes during the window, falling back to the old key.
defects.failure: Mid-rollout, a copy of the previous release records a transfer with memo 'rent'; the new release's API and export show it with an empty memo.
defects.head: e54bd9eabcfdc0e0ba5b6f946f16b6c1c2e31517

defects.title: Interest is rounded to a hundredth of a cent, so balances stop being whole cents
defects.summary: dailyInterest multiplies by 100 and divides by 100 as if the amount were dollars, so it rounds to two decimal places of a cent: $1,000 at 5% earns 13.7 cents a day, not 14. Balances become fractional, against the rule that amounts are whole cents. The PR updates the tests' expected values to 13.7 and 100013.7 without remark.
defects.failure: An account of $1,000 at 5%: one day's interest makes the balance 100013.7 cents; the API, the export and every later calculation carry the fraction.
defects.head: f278b0c346ce2ad4e6fb68b3654f61ff3181657f

defects.title: The freeze webhook is sent before the ownership check, so any member can freeze anyone's card
defects.summary: The freeze route notifies the card processor first and only then calls freezeAccount, which checks ownership. A member who posts a freeze for someone else's account gets a 404, but the account.freeze-requested event has already gone out with that account's id. docs/security.md: authorise before any observable effect, webhooks included.
defects.failure: Member O posts POST /accounts/<member M's account>/freeze: the answer is 404, and the card processor receives account.freeze-requested for M's account.
defects.head: 1cac44578f11f347ba81a0079de446337b81b27d

clean.title: Webhooks: a delivery id for de-duplicating retries
clean.head: e9f6f76a791dd86f98ab91c01dc31dc5004a3cfe

known.title: Tokens are compared with === and stored in plain text
No rate limiting on any route
newId is unique within one process only
Concurrent saves in one process share one temp file
known.note: On main since the first commit: save() names its temp file from the process id alone, so two requests saving at once write the same temp file and race on the rename; one can fail or publish the other's half-written content. Found, and marked pre-existing, by the 0.4.0 review of #8.

known.title: CSV cells with a bare carriage return are not quoted
known.note: True about main: csvCell quotes a cell for a comma, a quote or a newline, not for a lone carriage return, and a memo may carry one (any string of at most 140 characters), so an export can carry a row a reader splits in two. Reported pre-existing by the Codex benchmark on the clean PR #11.

adjudicated.title: New currency test never varies the currency value
adjudicated.note: False. A transfer's two accounts must share a currency, so both are NZD by necessity; the test uses the non-default currency precisely so that code which forgets to read the account (writing undefined, '' or the AUD default) fails. The only code it cannot distinguish is one that hard-codes 'NZD', which is not a plausible defect. No failure scenario beyond the test's own purpose.

adjudicated.title: New onBehalfOf test never checks who gets attributed
adjudicated.note: True. The test asserts status codes and the balance and never reads the transfer row or the audit entry, so it is blind to D6. A reviewer would ask for an attribution assertion. It is the test gap of D6, not a second defect.

adjudicated.title: Overdraft test checks status only, misses persistence
adjudicated.note: True. The HTTP test asserts only the status of the overdraft route, never the body or a follow-up read, so it is blind to D4. Severity overstated: a test gap is not critical in itself; the defect it hides is.

adjudicated.title: canCover test bypasses store, misses lost overdraft
adjudicated.note: True. canCover is unit-tested with a hand-built object, so the store's stripping of overdraftCents is never exercised. The test gap of D4; same note on severity.

adjudicated.title: Literal JSON null body crashes the export route (500)
adjudicated.note: True. readJson returns JSON.parse's value as is, so a body of the literal text null makes body === null and `const { name } = body` throws, answered as a 500 instead of a 400. Introduced at this line by the PR; the same class exists on main for /transfers, which destructures its body too, so it is a fair medium rather than a new vulnerability.

adjudicated.title: Paged transfers test can't detect the off-by-one slice bug
adjudicated.note: True. The paging test uses three transfers, below PAGE_SIZE, so it passes with either slice end. The test gap of D1. Severity overstated for a test gap; the defect it hides is high.

adjudicated.title: Withdrawal never re-checks /summary after mutating totals
adjudicated.note: True. The HTTP test reads the summary after the deposit and only the balance after the withdrawal, so it is blind to D9. The test gap of D9.

adjudicated.title: Withdraw's closed-account 409 path is never tested
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. The statement is true, but the finding itself verified the code is correct; an untested correct path has no failure scenario, and the skill defines a finding as a defect with one. A coverage note, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Control regex misses C1 and Unicode line separators
adjudicated.note: True. The PR's own rule is one printable line; U+0080–U+009F are control characters and U+2028/U+2029 are line separators, and all pass the ASCII-only regex into storage and the CSV, where csvCell quotes only on comma, quote and newline. Severity overstated: medium, not high.

adjudicated.title: seed script still passes label, not name
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted: renaming openAccount's parameter from label to name also broke scripts/seed.mjs in this PR (it now throws 'label is required'), the same class of defect planted as D3 in PR #3. The author's accident, caught by the review. Severity: medium, as D3 is rated; critical overstates a seed script.

adjudicated.title: No test ever has ownerId differ from actor
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. True that nothing exercises the new ownerId override, but the override is correct and nothing fails; a coverage note on correct code, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Audit test's single transfer never exercises recipient-side or cross-account scoping
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. The route is correct (the finding does not claim otherwise); the test could be stronger, but an untested correct path has no failure scenario. A coverage note, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Audit route scans the entire global collection, unpaginated
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. Every list in this service scans its in-memory collection; the audit route does what listAccounts and transfersFor do, on a JSON-file store that is whole in memory by design. No failure at any scale the service is built for; the response stays bounded to the account. A design remark, rated low by the review itself.

adjudicated.title: Accountant can close and export any account
adjudicated.note: True. The accountant test exercises the two read routes only, so it is blind to D5. The test gap of D5, worded as the defect itself; critical overstates a test gap.

adjudicated.title: POST /accounts crashes to 500 on JSON null body
adjudicated.note: True. Before this PR the route spread the body (`{ ...body, … }`), which tolerates null; the rewrite reads `body.label` directly, so a literal null JSON body throws and answers 500 instead of 400. Introduced at this line by the PR; the same class as the null-body finding on #7. Medium is fair.

adjudicated.title: Production entrypoint never wires a real fraud screen
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. The PR says transfers of $1,000 or more are now screened by the fraud service, but the entrypoint builds createServer(store, { webhook }) with no screen, so the running service uses the allow-everything default and screens nothing. The description mentions the default but not that production uses it. Severity overstated: the feature is inert rather than harmful, so medium, not critical.

adjudicated.title: ListCache entries grow without bound or eviction
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. The list cache keys on owner and page, and an entry leaves only when the same key is read after expiry or the owner is forgotten. A signed-in user who walks ?page=1, 2, 3 and so on adds an entry per page, each kept for good. Main's single-account cache caches only accounts that exist, so it is bounded. Medium is fair.

adjudicated.title: Hourly in-process save auto-clobbers concurrent writes
adjudicated.note: True, narrow. Before the PR an idle copy never wrote; the timer now saves every hour whether or not anything changed, so during the two-copy window docs/deploy.md describes, an idle copy overwrites the other copy's writes with its stale state. It extends the README's known one-process limitation rather than creating a new class, and it is confined to the deploy window: high overstates it. The Codex benchmark reported the same-process race at line 164: the timer's save and a request handler's save can overlap, both writing the one temporary file `<file>.<pid>.tmp` before renaming it, so one rename can move a file the other is still writing. Same hazard, true. The Claude-via-runner benchmark reported it at line 162 as well; `finding` keeps this ruling to the race findings at these lines.

adjudicated.title: Old binary's writes silently erase lastAccruedOn mid-deploy
adjudicated.note: True, narrow. A copy of the previous release strips lastAccruedOn, a key its SCHEMA does not list, from any account it writes during the rollout; a new copy that starts from that file mid-window sees the guard empty and its hourly job credits the account a second time that day. Needs a restart inside the window: low, not high. The Codex benchmark reported the same mechanism at the SCHEMA line (store.js:12) as a rollback hazard: a rolled-back copy strips the key from every account it writes, and the next roll-forward credits again. Same defect, true.

adjudicated.title: Cache-hit path never retries or confirms durable save
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. remember() records the key and its 201 before store.save(); if the save fails, the first request answers 500 but a retry with the same key answers 201 from memory for a transfer not yet on disk, lost if the process stops before another save. An idempotency record belongs after the commit. Needs a failed save: medium, not high.

adjudicated.title: Owner webhook equal to operator's causes duplicate delivery
adjudicated.note: True, low, and not the planted defect though it sits on one of its lines. notify() sends to [url, ...also] without removing duplicates, so an owner who sets the operator's own endpoint makes it receive each of that account's events twice.

adjudicated.title: Literal JSON null body crashes /webhook with 500
adjudicated.note: True, medium, and not the planted defect though it sits in its route. The new route reads body.url before any shape check, so a literal null body answers 500 instead of 400; the same class as the null-body findings on #7 and #9.

adjudicated.title: publicAccount never serializes frozen state
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. The PR adds frozenAt but publicAccount lists no field for it, though it shows closed: the freeze route answers with an account that looks unfrozen, a member cannot see that a card is frozen, and an administrator cannot find frozen accounts to unfreeze. Medium, not high.

adjudicated.title: Rollback silently unfreezes accounts
adjudicated.note: True, narrow. A copy of the previous release strips frozenAt, which its SCHEMA does not list, from any account it writes, during the rollout window or after a rollback, so a frozen card goes live again without a record. The same mechanism as #14's lastAccruedOn finding; worse here because it undoes a security action. Narrow but not low: medium.

adjudicated.title: POST /accounts 500s on a null JSON body
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. The refactor replaced `{ ...body, … }`, which tolerates null, with `body.label` and `body.currency`, so a literal null JSON body throws and answers 500 instead of 400. Introduced by this PR; the same class as the null-body findings on #7 and #9. Medium is fair.

adjudicated.title: actingFor lets an admin impersonate any user, not just members
adjudicated.note: True, low, and not planted. The PR and README say an administrator acts on a member's behalf, but actingFor checks only the caller's role, so an administrator can act as another administrator or an accountant. Only that user's own accounts can move, which limits the harm; with D6 the act is recorded under the other administrator's name. High overstates it.

adjudicated.title: No reconciliation path for totals drift across a rollback
adjudicated.note: True, medium, and not planted. The running total is kept only by the new code, and migration 003 builds it once. During the rollout window docs/deploy.md describes, and after any rollback, copies of the previous release take deposits without bumping it, and nothing ever recomputes it from the accounts: the summary stays wrong for good. Separate from D9, which is the new code's own withdrawals.

adjudicated.title: Null overdraft body returns 500
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted. The new overdraft route reads body.overdraftCents without checking that the parsed body is an object, so a literal null JSON body answers 500 instead of 400: the same class as the null-body findings on #3, #7, #9 and #16. Found by the Codex benchmark. Medium is fair.

adjudicated.title: Accepted names can create no file; Unicode characters are miscounted
adjudicated.note: True, low. The length check counts UTF-16 units and accepts names that are not file names (a NUL byte, a Windows device name), so a name the API accepts can fail to create a CSV, and a 33-character name of emoji is refused as too long. Two findings from the Codex benchmark at this line; both hold, neither matters much.

adjudicated.title: Body errors bypass sign-in warnings
adjudicated.note: True, low. The body is parsed before requireUser runs, so a request with a bad token and a malformed body is refused with 400 and never logged as a failed sign-in, which the PR added the warning for. Found by the Codex benchmark.

adjudicated.title: Cutover recredits already-paid accounts
adjudicated.note: True, low; reported high. The migration marks every account as never credited, so on the cutover day an account the operator's daily job already credited is credited once more by the first hourly run: one day's interest, once per account, when the old job ran that day before the deploy. Found by the Codex benchmark.

adjudicated.title: Restart loops prevent all accrual
adjudicated.note: True, low; reported high. Nothing runs at start-up, so a copy that never stays up for an hour never accrues, and a restart loop or an hourly deploy cadence starves the job silently. One immediate run fixes it. Found by the Codex benchmark.

adjudicated.title: Accrual exceptions crash the server
adjudicated.note: True, low; reported medium. The timer callback guards only the save's rejection; a synchronous throw from accrueInterest would escape it and end the process. Nothing in accrueInterest is known to throw, so this is a missing guard rather than a failure anyone has produced. Found by the Codex benchmark.

adjudicated.title: Failed accrual remains only in memory
adjudicated.note: False. The store is one in-memory object written whole: after a failed save, memory stays ahead of disk until the next save, from the next request or the next hour, exactly as for every request handler's write. If the process dies first, the credit and its marker are lost together and the next run credits again. A design observation about the service, not a defect of the PR. Reported by the Codex benchmark; `finding` keeps this ruling off the race reported at the same line.

adjudicated.title: Hourly job blocks event loop under load
adjudicated.note: False. The ledger is one process over an in-memory JSON store, and everything it does is synchronous on the event loop: every route scans or updates the store inline, and every save serialises the whole file. The hourly loop costs microseconds per account, less than the save that follows it and that every request already pays. A design observation about the service, not a defect of the PR. Reported by the Claude-via-runner benchmark.
